transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-12-13
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: 46m
Attendees: Oliver Hayes (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood Solutions), Jared Kim (Pelican CTO), Priya Desai (Pelican ML Lead), Luca Moreno (Pelican DevOps), Anya Petrova (Pelican PM)

Summary: Intro/discovery focus on selecting an open model and deployment mode. Customer needs long-context multi-lingual support, tool-calling for internal retrieval + external APIs, and enterprise security. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted, dedicated, and private. Redwood to share benchmarks + pilot SOW.

---
[00:00:10] Oliver: Hi everyone, thanks for taking the time, I'm Oliver from Redwood, i have Maya and Diego with me, uh Maya will cover the technical model selection stuff, Diego on solutions and deployment options.
[00:00:22] Jared: Hey Oliver, thanks. Quick intro I'm Jared, CTO at Pelican, we build long-form financial research summarization across EN/ES/PT, and we're evaluating hosting options.
[00:00:28] Priya: Priya here Priya: ML lead, mostly concerned with model quality on Spanish and Portuguese, and also cost.
[00:00:33] Luca: Luca, infra, i'll own networking and KMS stuff.
[00:00:36] Anya: Anya, PM, i'll track success criteria and timelines.
[00:00:40] Oliver: Awesome. Quick agenda: 1) current infra and constraints, 2) model needs (context, multilingual, tool-calling), 3) hosted vs dedicated vs private tradeoffs, 4) next steps and pilot. Sound good?
[00:00:48] Jared: Yep.

[00:01:20] Maya: Cool, i'll jump into model-level questions first, what's your typical document length and context need? You mentioned long docs in the invite.
[00:01:29] Priya: Yeah, most of our research pieces are 30 30-80k tokens, often with appendices. For summarization and Q&A we need at least 64k context, ideally up to 128k for full-doc ingest.
[00:01:42] Maya: Got it, 64k minimum. That steers model choice not every open model supports efficient 64/128k context out of the box. We also need to know expected request patterns (interactive vs batched).
[00:01:52] Jared: Interactive, mostly mostly analysts ask questions and expect sub-second-ish responses
[00:02:04] Diego: To clarify, sub-second for short spans
[00:02:08] Priya: Correct.

[00:02:35] Maya: On multilingual
[00:02:41] Priya: EN 65%, ES 25%, PT 10%. We need models that don't degrade on ES/PT.

[00:03:10] Oliver: Are you leaning toward hosted for speed to market or do you already have compliance requirements pushing Dedicated/Private?
[00:03:18] Jared: We're a regulated partner to some banks, so SOC2 is a must. Initially we'd consider Hosted if the data never leaves encrypted boundaries and retention is configurable, but we might need Dedicated or Private for audit controls and KMS/HSM integration
[00:04:05] Diego: On KMS
[00:04:11] Luca: For pilot we can use managed keys, but production we'll need our own KMS (AWS KMS + custom rotation). Also VPC peering or private link is required.

[00:04:42] Maya: Good notes. Now model comparisons
[00:05:00] Priya: Which ones have best multilingual out of those?
[00:05:04] Maya: Mistral performs well for EN, but its Spanish/Portuguese isn't as battle-tested as some Llama3 variants that had multi-lingual reweights. Llama3 34B reweights (community forks) can be strong if you want consistent ES/PT. There are tradeoffs in latency/cost
[00:05:28] Jared: What about tool calling? We need the model to support function/tool calling so it can call our retrieval microservice and optionally call external APIs.
[00:05:36] Maya: Most of the open families support function-calling style via the inference layer
[00:06:00] Priya: Are there recommended fine-tuned variants for tool-calling?
[00:06:03] Maya: Yes
[00:06:30] [00:06:30] Speaker 1: mm-hmm, okay.

[00:06:45] Diego: Let's talk throughput and batching
[00:07:02] Luca: For our SLAs, tail latency consistency is important. How does Redwood handle fallbacks if a model variant is overloaded?
[00:07:10] Maya: We have smart routing and automated fallback to compatible variants (e.g., quantized or smaller model) to keep requests served. We also do KV caching/prefix caching to reduce repeated context costs. Note: sometimes transcripts show K V cash

[00:07:45] Priya: Quantization will affect quality; we need to see quality impact on our Spanish prompts.

[00:08:30] Oliver: Can you share your success criteria / eval metrics? For example, what accuracy or ROUGE/QA pass rates are you targeting?
[00:08:38] Anya: For summaries we want 85%+ human acceptance on a blind review, and for QA retrieval accuracy > 90% on our NIST-style bench. Latency targets we stated earlier. Cost target is under $0.02 per 1k tokens end-to-end (rough ballpark) but that's flexible if quality is significantly better.

[00:09:15] Maya: Great. On context/manage long docs: options are 1) use a model with native 128k support, 2) chunk+retrieve with a retrieval layer and tool-calling, 3) use KV cache and prefix caching. For full doc summarize, many customers chunk then do a synthesis pass with the model. If you want single-context full-doc ops, we'll test 64k/128k variants in the pilot.

[00:09:54] Priya: We prefer single-context when possible to avoid retrieval hallucinations, but we know cost goes up.

[00:10:10] Diego: On the pilot logistics
[00:10:20] Jared: Yes. Will you need infra credentials, or do we just give a GCS/S3 bucket and sample data?
[00:10:26] Maya: A shared bucket and a small test account is fine. For Dedicated pilot we'll spin reserved capacity. We'll also need network info for Private options later.

[00:11:05] Luca: Security
[00:11:12] Oliver: Yes, Redwood is SOC2 Type II; we'll share the security pack. Logs can be retained per-customer policy; we support audit logs, token-level cost breakdowns, and you can configure retention. For Private deployments we can integrate with your KMS and provide full control.

[00:11:40] Luca: Also need SSO (SAML) and RBAC for Console.
[00:11:44] Oliver: Yep, SAML + SCIM and fine-grained RBAC supported. We'll add that to the security doc.

[00:12:15] Priya: For multilingual QA, do you do targeted fine-tuning or prefer instruction-tuning + retrieval?
[00:12:23] Maya: We can support both. Often customers start with instruction-tuned open models + retrieval; then if needed we do a small domain-tuning step (few-shot/fine-tune) for consistent Spanish/Portuguese behavior. That would be part of a later phase.

[00:12:50] Jared: Any customer references with similar constraints? Long context + banking/regulatory?
[00:12:55] Oliver: We have a couple anonymized refs in finance

[00:13:20] Diego: On cost modeling
[00:13:24] Oliver: Very rough: hosted pay-as-you-go can be 20-40% higher per-token for peak interactive unless you commit; Dedicated reserved capacity brings unit cost down significantly for steady throughput. Private is similar to Dedicated but with platform fee and potentially infra costs you'd absorb. We'll include ballpark numbers in the pricing doc.

[00:13:55] Priya: For model families, can we run Mistral and Llama3 in parallel for the pilot?
[00:14:00] Maya: Yes, we typically test 3 candidates: a smaller Mistral variant (cost-effective), a mid-size Llama3 34B for multilingual quality, and a quantized Llama3 70B tuned for long context if you want to push limits. We'll pick specific checkpoints based on the benchmark.

[00:14:50] Luca: Network question
[00:14:57] Diego: We support both VPC peering and private link; we'll share the network requirements doc. Usually it's outbound TLS to our endpoints plus a private peering route when Dedicated/Private is used.

[00:15:30] Priya: Regarding function calling
[00:15:37] Maya: Yes, Redwood's runtime supports structured function calls, return-of-objects, and chaining. We'll share a demo repo and a short runbook. It includes examples for RAG where the model calls retrieval, receives documents, and then synthesizes an answer with citations.

[00:16:10] Jared: About latency
[00:16:18] Maya: Sure
[00:16:55] Priya: Any limitations we should be aware of for 128k?
[00:16:59] Maya: 128k support exists but is more expensive and fewer open checkpoints have native 128k. We'll test native long-context variants vs chunk+retrieve to see tradeoffs. Some models degrade on long context unless they were explicitly trained for it.

[00:17:30] Oliver: Let's capture success criteria again
[00:17:33] Anya: 1) 85%+ human accept rate on summaries across EN/ES/PT, 2) median latency <500ms for short queries, 3) pilot cost estimate within 20% of projected budget, 4) KMS + SOC2 compliance check.

[00:18:20] Diego: Anything else on tooling
[00:18:25] Priya: We use Pinecone and internal vector store. We need connector work.

[00:18:32] Maya: We have prebuilt connectors for Pinecone and common vector DBs, and for internal stores we can use a retrieval microservice invoked via function call.

[00:19:25] Oliver: Next steps recap: we'll share benchmark spreadsheet, security pack, pricing, and a pilot SOW. You'll share sample prompts and confirm KMS details.

[00:20:00] Jared: Quick question
[00:20:05] Maya: Yes, we run QA/regression tests tied to prompt sets and monitor hallucination metrics; part of Redwood Optimize is regression alerts. We'll include those eval templates in the deck.

[00:20:35] Luca: On data residency
[00:20:41] Oliver: Yes, region pinning is supported for Dedicated/Private; hosted has region options in our cloud but dedicated gives you deterministic location.

[00:21:10] Priya: Any gotchas with function-calling and streaming? We want partial outputs while the model calls tools sometimes.
[00:21:17] Maya: Streaming with function-calling is supported; you can stream chunks of the structured response. Edge cases exist when the model triggers multiple calls in a chain

[00:21:50] Jared: For benchmarking, will you include cost estimates for quantized paths?
[00:21:55] Maya: Yes, we'll report latency/quality/cost across fp16, int8, and dynamic quantization.

[00:22:30] Diego: Who will be our main Redwood contacts?
[00:22:33] Oliver: Myself for commercial, Maya for tech, Diego for deployment.

[00:23:05] Priya: One more
[00:23:12] Maya: Yes

[00:23:45] Anya: Timeline
[00:23:52] Oliver: Yes

[00:24:40] Jared: Anything else from your side?
[00:24:44] Maya: Not from me; just to emphasize we'll test 3 model candidates, quant levels, and report per-lang quality. Also we recommend a small domain-tuning pass if the initial bench shows ES/PT gaps.

[00:25:35] Diego: I have a couple infra follow-ups after the call; i'll ping Diego Ramos.

[00:26:10] Diego Ramos: Sounds good
